plan.coverage_explanation: Tests repeated door-state cycles and requires event-log output during each cycle. Each cycle contains both electrical transitions, so the test does not prescribe the unspecified door-contact polarity. This covers a necessary part of opening-event logging, but does not independently establish log attribution or position contents. The temperature limit, transport-state definition, GPS input syntax, display alternation period, counter presentation, vibration polarity, and alarm/reset policy are unspecified; consequently those behaviors cannot be asserted reliably with this finite suite.
assumptions: The system is operating as a transport monitor after setup; no separate transport-enable input or command is specified.
The door contact has two binary states. Each complete LOW/HIGH cycle includes an opening regardless of contact polarity. Both states are held long enough for ordinary debouncing.
No GPS command syntax is invented or injected. Position formatting and behavior without a GPS fix are not checked.
Bench defaults apply to the D13 LED: active HIGH with a resistor to GND. D6 is treated as a passive tone-driven buzzer.
LM35 conversion uses 10 mV per degree Celsius and the bench default 5 V ADC reference. The application temperature upper limit is missing and is not asserted.

The reference chooses an 8 C upper limit, an active-LOW door contact using INPUT_PULLUP, active-LOW vibration pulses, a two-second display alternation, and non-latching alarms. These are illustrative choices for unspecified parameters, not acceptance constraints.
For the reference only, each received serial line or idle-delimited message is retained verbatim as the simulated position. No candidate GPS grammar is required by the checks.
